One-line judgment: childcare workers are not just minding children, but attending to children at schools, businesses, private households and childcare institutions and performing tasks such as dressing, feeding, bathing and overseeing play - the official scope is Attend to children at schools, businesses, private households, and childcare
institutions. Perform a variety of tasks, such as dressing, feeding, bathing, and overseeing play., and O*NET separately lists Nannies (39-9011.01). In daily work they maintain a safe play environment (importance 92); observe and monitor children's play activities (87); communicate with parents or guardians about daily activities and behaviour and related problems (85); support children's emotional and social development and encourage understanding of others and a positive self-concept (84); care for children in institutional settings such as group homes, nurseries and private businesses or schools for people with disabilities (84); sanitize toys and play equipment (83); dress children and change diapers (83); keep records for each child including daily observations and activities and meals and
medication information (82); identify signs of emotional or developmental problems in children and bring them to parents' or guardians' attention (81); instruct children in health and personal habits such as eating, resting and toilet habits (80); organize and store toys and materials to keep activity areas tidy and orderly (80); perform general administrative tasks such as attendance and internal paperwork and telephone calls (79); develop curriculum plans suited to the developmental stage (77); perform housekeeping duties such as laundry, cleaning, dishwashing and changing linens (77); read to children and teach simple painting, handicrafts and songs (76); help prepare food and serve meals and snacks (76); discipline children and take other behaviour management measures (74); regulate children's rest periods (71); and organize and take part in recreational activities and outings such as games and field trips (70). Additional tasks include sanitizing bottles and preparing formula (80), helping children with homework (79), providing care for children with physical or developmental or mental health conditions (79), performing general personnel functions such as
supervision and training and scheduling (71), and accompanying children to and from school and on outings and to medical appointments (61). O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation), SVP range below 6.0, with interest codes SA (Social, Artistic); the education distribution is high school or equivalent 39%, associate's or other two-year degree 23% and less than high school
14%. The core boundary is that this is a position centred on care safety, daily care, age-appropriate activities and record keeping and communication, and it is not the same as a kindergarten teacher, a special education teacher or medical staff; this page does not write the licensing and background check requirements of U.S. states and institutions up as a universal threshold, nor does it write mainland China's childcare institution standards up as a uniform national standard.

Signals to keep exploring: you can maintain line-of-sight supervision and patience over the long term, are willing to look after several children at the same time and handle sudden emotions and conflict, and are willing to write up each day's observations and anomalies as traceable records; the O*NET work context shows that 83% of respondents in this occupation have ongoing contact with others, 81% have face-to-face discussions every day, 65% consider collaboration with a work team extremely important, 51% work at a very close physical distance, 77%
work indoors in a controlled environment every day, 48% stand about half of the work hours and 24% stand continuously, 31% encounter conflict situations every day, 32% have to deal with unpleasant or angry or discourteous people more than weekly, 40% are exposed to disease or infection every day, 28% are exposed to minor burns or cuts or bites or stings every day, 42% have very high responsibility for the health and safety of others and 26% high responsibility, 47% make decisions every day, 54%
have some freedom in how they decide, 61% have a typical work week of 40 hours and 32% less than 40 hours, 93% have a regular schedule, and 16% of the work is highly automated while 66% is not automated at all. These figures show that the job spends most of its time on close-range care, communication and safety supervision, that physical, infection and emotional pressure are real, and that it is managed through staff ratios, environment checks and escalation procedures.

Conditions for pausing before a large investment: you have not yet completed, under supervision, a full loop from handover and authorization confirmation to checking the register and staff ratio, inspecting the environment and toys and equipment, carrying out eating and hygiene and rest care, observing and recording status and anomalies, and
reporting and handing over under procedure; or you cannot maintain line-of-sight supervision and patience over the long term; or you are unwilling to report and record anomalies and incidents under the institution's procedures. Do not ignore safety and hygiene and record keeping just because you like children: one of the key tasks of this occupation is maintaining a safe play environment (importance
92) and keeping meal and medication records for each child. If you would rather do curriculum design and systematic teaching, a kindergarten teacher is a similar position with different qualifications and duties; if you want to do diagnosis and treatment, you should take the medical and psychological qualification path.

Education, qualifications and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation), SVP range below 6.0; the education distribution on this occupation's page is high school or equivalent 39%, associate's or other two-year degree 23% and less than high school
14%. In the United States, entry education and training requirements vary with the state and the setting and the family arrangement, from no formal education to early childhood certification; licensing, background checks and training requirements differ for centre-based care, family care, self-employment and school positions. The O*NET certification directory lists certificates such as the Child Development Associate (awarded by the Council for Professional
Recognition) and the Certified Childcare Professional (awarded by the National Early Childhood Program Accreditation). In mainland China, the national occupational skill standard for childcare workers defines skill levels, but the training reference hours are not directly tied to promotion; working in a childcare institution also requires meeting institutional and health and no-abuse and no-criminal-record requirements, which must be confirmed under the applicable regulations and local rules. This page does not push the licensing or registration requirements of one jurisdiction onto another, nor does it write training certificates up as a practice qualification. Education background, professional certification, statutory and practice qualifications, and institutional authorization are four different things.

In one line: this is a position that turns whether line-of-sight supervision was continuous, whether the staff ratio and the register match, whether the environment and toys and meals were checked under procedure, whether eating and hygiene and rest were cared for as needed, whether anomalies and incidents were reported under procedure, and whether records and parent communication can be reviewed into traceable evidence; the outputs are care and handover records, daily observation and development records, activity and curriculum plans, meal and medication and sleep records, incident and anomaly reporting and handling records, and parent and guardian communication records; it is not the systematic teaching position of a kindergarten teacher, nor the diagnostic and treatment position of medical staff, and it does not replace the institution's head or the competent authorities in determining childcare qualifications and safety responsibility.

The work of childcare workers can be divided into three connected but distinct work dimensions. The first is care and safety supervision: confirm authorization and the register at handover, check the on-duty staff ratio, inspect the environment and toys and equipment, carry out eating and hygiene and rest care, maintain line-of-sight supervision continuously and observe the children's condition, and handle anomalies immediately under procedure. The second is daily activities and early development support: choose age-appropriate activities, organize games and reading and handicrafts, guide self-care and daily routines, support emotional and social development, and record developmental observations. The third is records and communication and safety escalation: keep records for each child, communicate with parents or guardians about daily activities and behaviour, bring signs of emotional or developmental problems to parents' attention promptly, and complete handover and reporting under the institution's process. The three work dimensions share one bottom line: safety and authorization come first, and no activity may be allowed to sacrifice line-of-sight supervision.
Ensure every child is always under line-of-sight supervision in a safe environment

Handover and authorization confirmation, check the register and staff ratio, inspect the environment and toys and equipment, carry out eating and hygiene and rest care, observe and record the children's condition and anomalies, report and hand over under procedure
Use age-appropriate activities to support early development and emotional and social growth

Understand the age and developmental stage, design or select appropriate activities and curriculum, organize games and reading and handicrafts, guide self-care and daily routines, observe participation and interaction, record developmental observations and communicate with parents

Maintain each child's daily observation and activity and meal and medication records; communicate with parents or guardians about daily activities and behaviour and related problems; identify signs of emotional or developmental problems and bring them to parents' attention; sanitize toys and equipment and guide health and hygiene habits; when an incident or anomaly occurs, report and hand over under the institution's procedures and keep records; do not change pickup authorization or medication arrangements without authorization, and handle matters involving safety and health under the institution's rules.

Common adjacent positions include kindergarten teachers, special education teachers, teaching assistants, nannies and preschool and childcare institution managers. The key to judging the boundary is not the title but who is responsible for the curriculum and teaching assessment, who carries out diagnosis and treatment, who is responsible for the institution's qualifications and primary safety responsibility, and who carries out daily care and safety supervision and record keeping. The O*NET/SOC and the O*NET page for this occupation define 39-9011.00
as attending to children at schools and businesses and private households and childcare institutions and performing tasks such as dressing and feeding and bathing and overseeing play, and separately list Nannies (39-9011.01); on that basis this page distinguishes childcare workers from teaching positions that carry systematic teaching, and does not merge teaching or medical duties into this occupation.
The core purpose of the occupation differs

Childcare includes life care, play and early development support and may include developing age-appropriate curriculum plans; kindergarten teachers focus on organized care and education, and the tasks of the two overlap. China's Preschool Education Law requires play as the basic activity and prohibits primary-school-style teaching, and does not equate kindergarten teachers with positions that involve academic examinations.
The main work object and basis differ

The basis for the position includes the children's condition, knowledge of age-appropriate development, applicable regulations, institutional procedures and the guardian's lawful instructions; parental consent does not replace statutory obligations, staffing requirements or professional qualifications. Teachers and childcare workers may both work from age-appropriate activity plans; medical diagnosis and treatment is checked separately against the scope of practice.
The core process differs

Care positions emphasize handover, continuous supervision, life care, age-appropriate activities and records; teachers also observe and care, and it is not only about teaching and academic assessment. Kindergarten care and education centre on play and physical and mental development, and duties are allocated according to the actual position.
The main outputs differ

Common care records include observations, meals, sleep, approved medication, handover and anomaly reports, and may also include age-appropriate activity or curriculum plans; teachers also have lesson plans, observations and development portfolios, so no absolute boundary is drawn by the name of the material.
The division of responsibility differs

On-duty staff carry the actual care, supervision and record-keeping obligations; the operator, the institution, the person in charge and other staff each bear responsibility under the law and their duties, and the responsibility of the person in charge cannot be used to exempt individual obligations. Family childcare providers may also provide care themselves; medical diagnosis and treatment requires the corresponding qualification, and a teaching qualification does not replace care staffing.
Entry and licensing requirements differ

U.S. OOH: education, training and licensing vary with the state, the setting and the employer; some states require no education to start and employers often prefer high school. Many states require a licence for centres (including home-based childcare), and staff often need background checks, immunization records and minimum training, with some states requiring CPR and first aid. The education of nannies in private households is not set uniformly by the state, and Head Start positions have their own specific conditions; all settings cannot be written as one threshold. China: Articles 37/39 of the Preschool Education Law set out the kindergarten teacher qualification and the state-prescribed education and vocational childcare training for childcare workers respectively; Articles 44/45 set out the checks for relevant illegal records in recruitment and the health examination before entry and every year after. Childcare for children under 3 is checked separately against the childcare standards, and kindergarten rules are not transplanted wholesale. Articles 5/9 of the measures on family childcare points set out the filing materials, experience or relevant professional background, childcare and mental health and food safety and first aid and fire safety training, health and the designated offence record conditions; these are not a unified ban on all offences or on all nannies in private households.
Boundaries of the conclusion

This page only compares the division of work between this occupation and its adjacent positions, and does not use it to judge whether an individual is suited to teaching or medical work, nor does it write the entry requirements of one jurisdiction up as a universal threshold in another; the specific position requirements must follow the latest rules of the recruiting institution and the local competent authorities.

Key occupational judgments revolve around six questions: whether safety supervision has ever lapsed, whether care was carried out under procedure, whether developmental observations have a basis, whether records and communication can be reviewed, whether anomalies and incidents were escalated under procedure, and whether authorization and boundaries were exceeded.
The key point of judgment one is whether supervision continuity and the staff ratio meet the requirement

Whether a qualifying adult is always present and maintaining line-of-sight supervision during the shift, whether staffing follows the ratio, and whether handovers have a register and authorization records; the first occupational judgment of a childcare worker is whether someone is watching every child right now, not whether the activity is exciting.
The key point of judgment two is whether care is carried out under procedure

Whether care such as eating and sleep and medication and toileting is carried out under the institution's procedures and the parents' authorization, and whether time and content records are kept; whether allergies and medication and special health conditions have been handed over under the institution's rules, without relying on verbal memory.
The key point of judgment three is whether observations and judgments have a basis

Repeated observation helps distinguish everyday changes from developmental signals, so record the observations and statements and bring them to the guardian's or the appropriate professional's attention; do not diagnose by yourself. Urgent health risks and suspected violations of minors' rights are not left until observation is repeated before being handled or reported.
The key point of judgment four is whether records can be reviewed

Article 13 of China's Personal Information Protection Law sets out consent, statutory obligations and emergency protection of life and health separately as bases for processing, and Articles 28 to 31 protect sensitive information and information on children under 14; kindergartens additionally check Article 21 of the Preschool Education Law. Check processing, access, retention and outbound transfer against the purpose, the jurisdiction and the actual lawful basis, and note that institutional permission, de-identification or an internal network does not by itself make processing lawful; statutory reporting and emergency protection must not be delayed by internal review.
The key point of judgment five is the escalation path for anomalies and incidents

Article 11 of China's Law on the Protection of Minors: units and their staff who have close contact with minors must, on discovering violations of minors' rights, suspected violations of those rights or other danger, report to the public security, civil affairs, education and other relevant departments immediately. Kindergartens additionally follow Article 52 of the Preschool Education Law to protect immediately and report to public security and education and other departments, and in an emergency to rescue and avoid danger immediately and report promptly and notify the parents or guardians; they must not wait for confirmation, internal approval or substitute internal reporting for statutory reporting. Communication should state the facts observed and measures taken, avoid assigning responsibility without a basis, and must not use a refusal to explain externally to block statutory notification.
The key point of judgment six is authorization and boundaries

Care, records, age-appropriate activities and communication are carried out according to duties; medication requires checking the position's qualification, the medical order or lawful instruction, the institution's rules and the necessary authorization, and there is no independent diagnosis or adjustment of medication or dosage; pickup requires checking identity and lawful authorization. Emergency rescue and lawful reporting do not wait for the head's approval.

In daily work they maintain a safe play environment; observe and monitor children's play activities; communicate with parents or guardians about daily activities and behaviour and related problems; support children's emotional and social development and encourage understanding of others and a positive self-concept;
care for children in institutional settings such as group homes and nurseries and private businesses or schools for people with disabilities; sanitize toys and play equipment and dress children and change diapers; keep records for each child including daily observations and activities and meals and medication information; identify signs of emotional or developmental problems and bring them to parents' or guardians' attention; instruct children in health and personal habits such as eating and resting and toilet habits; organize and store toys and materials; perform general administrative tasks such as attendance and internal paperwork and telephone calls; develop curriculum plans suited to
the developmental stage; perform housekeeping duties such as laundry and cleaning and dishwashing and changing linens; read to children and teach simple painting and handicrafts and songs; help prepare food and serve meals and snacks; discipline children and take behaviour management measures; regulate rest periods; and organize and take part in recreational activities and outings such as games and field trips; additional tasks include sanitizing bottles and preparing formula, helping children with homework, providing care for children with physical or developmental or mental health conditions, performing general personnel functions such as
supervision and training and scheduling, and accompanying children to and from school and on outings and to medical appointments. Responsibility boundary: the O*NET core tasks include developing age-appropriate curriculum plans (77), which cannot all be excluded as the teacher's authority; teacher, medical and childcare licensing are checked separately by jurisdiction. Childcare workers bear supervision, truthful recording and protection obligations according to their actual duties. Article 11 of China's Law on the Protection of Minors: units and their staff who have close contact with minors must, on discovering violations of minors' rights, suspected violations of those rights or other danger, report
immediately to the public security, civil affairs, education and other relevant departments. O*NET-SOC 39-9011.00 (Childcare Workers): Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation), SVP range below 6.0; interest codes SA (Social, Artistic); the official page lists 24 tasks (19 Core plus 5 Supplemental), with importance ranging from 92 (maintaining a safe play environment) to
61 (accompanying children to and from school and on outings and to medical appointments); the education distribution is high school or equivalent 39%, associate's or other two-year degree 23% and less than high school 14%; the occupation is marked as Bright Outlook and has 1 registered apprenticeship direction (Child Care Development
Specialist). The education percentages are U.S. respondents' answers about the requirements for newly hired staff, not a national recruitment share or a Chinese threshold; Bright
Outlook does not mean the growth rate is positive, and an apprenticeship example does not guarantee that enrolment is available locally. The O*NET occupational interest is SA, with the six types S86/A43/C41/R35/E29/I8 and 41 specific areas in the full table, led by social service 86, teaching 72 and personal service 61; this is a relative interest description of occupational tasks, not the type proportions of practitioners or an individual hiring threshold.

U.S. wages on the BLS OEWS May 2025 basis (shown on the O*NET page for this occupation, 39-9011.00): the annual 10th, 25th, median, 75th and 90th percentiles are 24,260, 29,360, 34,980, 38,570 and 46,010 USD; the same hourly percentiles are 11.66, 14.12, 16.82,
18.55 and 22.12 USD. The same BLS OOH page also gives an hourly median of 17.76 USD for other personal care and service workers and 24.51 USD for all occupations; this page uses the sub-item for this occupation and notes the existence of those two comparison bases, and does not treat a percentile as a starting salary or mix different bases. OEWS excludes the self-employed, employees of private households and agriculture and cannot represent all childcare pay.

NBS2025 annual averages of 70,226 yuan for non-private resident services, repair and other services and 79,857 yuan for social production and life service personnel in enterprises above designated size are backgrounds for different statistical populations and cannot be used to infer wages for this occupation. For childcare or education positions the corresponding categories can also be checked: health and social work non-private and private units 146,266/75,631 yuan, and education 133,539/63,908 yuan, both including other positions.
Use them according to the actual institution's industry, and do not map China from U.S. industry data; the national and regional wage distribution for this occupation in China remains insufficient evidence.

Current O*NET industry distribution: health care and social assistance 33%, other services (except public administration) 25%, educational services 13% and other 29%. The BLS U.S. SOC39-9011 projection is 1,010,300 people in 2025 to 990,400 people in 2035, a net decrease of 19,900 and a fall of 2% (whole number), with 150,300 openings per year on average over 2025—2035, all of them replacement needs from people moving to other occupations or leaving the labour
force. A projection is not year-by-year actual performance, the current hiring stock or AI causality. OOH2025 employment includes 24% self-employed and 17% private households, which differs from the OEWS wage sample that excludes both. OOH May 2025 industry hourly wages: local elementary and secondary schools 18.15, day care 16.43, and religious, grantmaking, civic, professional and similar organizations 16.23 USD, all for this occupation within the industry,
not a combined wage for all positions. The top three work activities are assisting and caring for others 80, decision making and problem solving 72 and thinking creatively 68, with communication 67 following.

of the work is not automated at all. Recruiting technology keywords are a market signal and do not equal proficiency, adoption or a long-term trend. entries.entity: O*NET-SOC 25-2011.00 Kindergarten Teachers (except special education) summary

paragraphs: Conclusion: these directions share with this occupation the underlying requirement of being child-centred and needing patience and a sense of responsibility, but they differ markedly in teaching and assessment responsibility, special education support, classroom assistance, the scale of the service setting, the institution's primary responsibility and collective care procedures.

The basis for comparison is the task and work activity descriptions on the O*NET-SOC 39-9011.00 page, the Nannies (39-9011.01) listed under see also on that page, the adjacent occupation list registered in this evidence route and the editorial notes on position boundaries; the entry requirements, practice qualifications and statutory authority of each position must be verified separately against its own page and the local regulations.

The table below compares positions and occupations adjacent to this occupation: kindergarten teachers, special education teachers, teaching assistants, nannies, preschool and childcare institution managers, and group childcare institution care positions. The four columns each answer the same kind of question: what this direction does, where the key difference from this occupation lies, and what kind of person is better suited to choosing it.
Deliver systematic teaching under a curriculum and assess learning outcomes
Kindergarten teachers design and deliver teaching under curriculum standards and syllabuses, with outputs mainly lesson plans, academic assessments and student development portfolios.
This occupation is mainly daily care and safety supervision and play interaction, and does not carry systematic teaching or academic assessment responsibility.

People who want to do curriculum design and systematic teaching and hold a teaching qualification are suited to being a kindergarten teacher; people who would rather provide care and companionship are suited to this occupation.
Provide specialized education and support for children with special needs
Special education teachers provide specialized teaching and support under an individualized education plan, with outputs mainly the individualized education plan and teaching records.
This occupation provides care and daily support for children with disabilities within the scope of authorization, and does not draw up individualized education plans or assess teaching.

People who want to do special education teaching and assessment are suited to being a special education teacher; people willing to accommodate individual needs in a care setting are suited to this occupation.
Assist teachers with classroom teaching and activity organization
Teaching assistants assist with classroom management and activity organization under the teacher's guidance, with outputs mainly classroom assistance and material preparation records.
This occupation's care recipients and settings are broader (including families and institutions and private households), while a teaching assistant's duties centre on classroom assistance.
People who want to enter a school teaching environment and gradually move towards a teacher position can start as a teaching assistant; people focused on care are suited to this occupation.
Provide one-to-one or small-scale care in private households
Nannies provide care in private households and take on the daily arrangements within the family, with outputs mainly care records and parent communication records.
O*NET lists nannies under see also for this occupation (Nannies, 39-9011.01), with the setting in private households and a smaller scale.

People who want to work in a one-to-one family setting are suited to being a nanny; people who want to work in an institutional setting with colleagues and procedural support are suited to this occupation.
Responsible for the operation and quality and primary safety responsibility of a childcare institution

including daily observations and meals and medication information (82), identifying signs of emotional or developmental problems and bringing them to parents' attention (81), instructing children in health and personal habits such as eating and resting and toilet habits (80), and organizing recreational activities and outings such as games and field trips (70). Care settings include schools, businesses, private households and childcare institutions.
entries.question: What do childcare workers do every day?

entries.answer:
The official scope limits this occupation to attending to children at schools and businesses and private households and childcare institutions and performing tasks such as dressing and feeding and bathing and overseeing play, and O*NET
separately lists Nannies (39-9011.01). Kindergarten teachers deliver systematic teaching under curriculum standards and assess learning outcomes; special education teachers provide specialized teaching and support under an individualized education plan; this occupation is mainly care safety and daily care and age-appropriate activities and record keeping and communication, does not carry systematic teaching or academic assessment responsibility and does not diagnose or treat.
entries.question: How is this position different from kindergarten teachers and special education teachers?

entries.answer: That cannot be inferred. The core tasks of this occupation are line-of-sight supervision, daily care, safety and hygiene and interpersonal interaction, and require people who are present to take responsibility. AI and digitalization change the way scheduling and records and notices are handled, and will not replace on-site supervision and safety judgments and parent communication. This page does not give a substitution rate or a disappearance year.
entries.question: Will childcare workers be replaced by AI?

entries.answer: The earlier affected parts are those that can be structured as inputs: schedule and attendance and staff ratio checking, generating and reminding on handover and inspection checklists, organizing observation and meal and medication and sleep records, and retrieving and summarizing parent notices and policy texts. The later affected parts are those that must be done by people present: line-of-sight supervision, on-site safety judgments, emotional soothing and emergency handling, and parent communication.

percentiles are 24,260, 29,360, 34,980, 38,570 and 46,010 USD. These are statistical positions, not an individual's starting salary or take-home pay; part-time work and self-employment are relatively common in this occupation, and the public statistics mainly cover employed positions.
entries.question: How much do childcare workers earn in the United States?

entries.answer:
O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation), SVP range below 6.0; the education distribution is high school or equivalent 39%, associate's or other two-year degree 23% and less than high school
14%. In the United States the entry requirements vary with the state and the setting and the family arrangement, from no formal education to early childhood certification, and usually include a background check. In mainland China the vocational skill standard for childcare workers defines skill levels, and childcare institutions have separate requirements on health and no abuse and no criminal record, with the specific requirements following the recruitment notice and the competent authorities' rules.
entries.question: What education and qualifications are needed to enter this occupation?

entries.answer:
Certification and licensing are two different things. The O*NET certification directory lists certificates such as the Child Development Associate (awarded by the Council for Professional Recognition) and the Certified Childcare Professional (awarded by the National Early
Childhood Program Accreditation); certification does not equal a licence, an employer appointment, signing authority or local authorization. In the United States, whether a licence is needed depends on the state and the institution type; teaching positions additionally require a teacher qualification, which is a different system from care positions.
entries.question: Do I need a licence or certification?

entries.answer: Changing jobs is usually not hard, because the education and experience thresholds for this occupation are relatively low; but three things have to be adapted to: a fixed schedule and high-intensity daily care, keeping records and handing over under institutional procedures, and handling conflict and anomalies under procedure. People with parenting, nursing, education or service industry experience usually pick it up more easily, but still need to complete the institution's safety and hygiene and information protection training.
entries.question: Is it hard to move over from other positions?

entries.answer:
It depends on your goal: if your goal is stable employment and continued accumulation in the care direction, this occupation has continuing demand for openings (BLS shows about 150,300 openings per year on average, all from replacement needs) and a clear path to class-leading and quality and management roles; but the income level of this occupation is relatively low among all occupations (hourly median 16.82
USD), and the physical and emotional load is real. Higher income usually requires moving towards a teacher qualification or institutional management.

description.text: Childcare workers attend to children at schools and businesses and private households and care institutions, with line-of-sight supervision, daily care, age-appropriate activities and record keeping and communication at the core: tasks and work context, the U.S. BLS wage and employment basis, mainland China statistical bases and gaps, and entry and qualification paths, risks and exercises all in one view.

subject.name: Childcare workers
subject.summary: Attend to children at schools, businesses, private households and childcare institutions: maintain line-of-sight supervision and the staff ratio, carry out eating and hygiene and sleep and medication care, use age-appropriate activities to support early development, maintain and write up children's records and communicate with parents, and handle and report anomalies under the institution's procedures.
